source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: R1-Zero: RL with GRPO and only rule-based rewards (answer correctness plus format) applied directly to a base model, no SFT. Pass@1 on AIME 2024 rose through training.
numbers: AIME 2024 pass@1 15.6% to 77.9%; with self-consistency (majority vote) 86.7%.
limits: Base is DeepSeek-V3-Base (685B MoE). Only the trajectory in the paper's figure is available.
agent_relevance: The reward is a checker, not a learned judge. Majority voting at inference adds about 9 points on top, which a scaffold can do without training.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: R1-Zero showed an 'aha moment': mid-training the model began to rethink with phrases like 'Wait, wait.' Response length grew through RL. R1-Zero also had poor readability and language mixing.
numbers: Reflection appears in an intermediate checkpoint (Table 2 of the paper).
limits: Presented from one example; later work (c06, c08) finds such behaviours already exist in base models.
agent_relevance: Self-reflection as a visible behaviour can be requested by a prompt or scaffold step; it is not unique to RL.
quote: Wait, wait. Wait. That's an aha moment I can flag here.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: Full R1 pipeline: cold-start SFT, reasoning RL with a language-consistency reward, rejection-sampling SFT, then RL for all scenarios. Final R1 matches o1-1217 on many tasks.
numbers: AIME 2024 pass@1: R1 79.8, o1-1217 78.1, R1-Zero 77.9; Codeforces rating 2029 (96.3 percentile); LiveCodeBench 65.9; SWE Verified 49.2; Aider-Polyglot 53.3.
limits: Self-reported by the lab; comparison to o1 depends on settings.
agent_relevance: Shows the ceiling of trained long reasoning. Our scaffold targets part of the gap through test-time structure.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: Negative results: the authors tried a process reward model (PRM) and Monte Carlo tree search and dropped both. PRM has three listed limits: hard to define fine steps, hard to label, reward hacking when model-based.
numbers: Qualitative section on unsuccessful attempts; no ablation numbers given.
limits: MCTS failed mainly because the token search space is huge and a value model is hard to train.
agent_relevance: Supports preferring hard, checkable verifiers over learned step judges.

source: Zeng et al. (2025) SimpleRL-Zoo: Investigating and Taming Zero RL for Open Base Models in the Wild
finding: Replicated zero-RL across 10 base models (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B/24B, DeepSeek-Math-7B, Qwen2.5 0.5B to 32B). Accuracy and length improved in most settings, but only with design care (format reward tuning, matching query difficulty to the model).
numbers: 10 base models; most improved. Qwen2.5 bases already follow instructions and self-reflect, so they are unrepresentative.
limits: Training dynamics differ by model family.
agent_relevance: Gains from RL depend on what the base already does; a prompt may be able to unlock the same behaviour.

source: Zeng et al. (2025) SimpleRL-Zoo: Investigating and Taming Zero RL for Open Base Models in the Wild
finding: First 'aha moment' (verification behaviour) seen in small models not from the Qwen family. Longer responses did not always come with more verification.
numbers: Seen in some small non-Qwen bases, not all.
limits: Keyword counting for verification is a proxy, not proof of real self-checking.
agent_relevance: Length is a poor quality signal; reward verified checks, not token count.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (Dr. GRPO)
finding: Base-model audit: Qwen2.5-Math models answer best with NO prompt template, hinting they saw question-answer text in pretraining. DeepSeek-V3-Base already shows 'aha' self-reflection before any RL.
numbers: Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B average over 5 math sets by template: R1 template 33.1, 4-shot 24.2, Qwen template 23.8, none 19.7 per my read of Table 1; the extracted table is garbled, so rows may be mis-aligned.
limits: Table 1 text extraction was messy; treat cell values as approximate.
agent_relevance: Template choice alone moves scores by about 10 points at the same weights, so baselines hide a big prompt effect.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (Dr. GRPO)
finding: GRPO has a length bias: dividing by response length makes long wrong answers get less penalty per token, so wrong outputs grow longer. Dr. GRPO removes the biased terms; incorrect responses get shorter and accuracy is kept.
numbers: Minimalist recipe: Qwen2.5-Math-7B reaches 43.3% on AIME 2024 using 27 hours on 8 A100 GPUs.
limits: Shown for Qwen2.5-Math; may not carry to other families.
agent_relevance: Growing 'thinking length' in RL can be an optimiser artefact. Longer chains are not proof of better reasoning.

source: Yue et al. (2025) Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
finding: Pass@k test across math, code and vision: RLVR models win at small k, but base models catch up and pass them at large k. RLVR sharpens sampling rather than adding capability.
numbers: Qwen2.5-32B on Minerva: base beats RL by about 9% at k=128. Oat-Zero and DAPO models start about 30% above base then are overtaken. Training-set pass@1 rises 26.1 to 42.5 while pass@256 falls with more steps.
limits: Mostly zero-RL on Qwen2.5 bases and public checkpoints; very long RL runs not tested (c17 disputes). Pass@256 can include lucky wrong-reasoning hits, so authors checked chains manually.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that samples and checks candidates exploits what the base already contains.
quote: base models consistently surpass RLVR models across all benchmarks and LLM families as k increases

source: Yue et al. (2025) Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
finding: Perplexity analysis: RLVR models' correct reasoning paths already have high likelihood under the base model. Distillation from a stronger teacher does widen the boundary.
numbers: Sampling-efficiency gap (base pass@256 minus RL pass@1) stays above 40 points for PPO, GRPO, Reinforce++, RLOO, ReMax and DAPO; GRPO 43.9 vs RLOO 42.6 on Omni-MATH in-domain. Problems RL solves but base never does are about 1% (about 5 on MATH500).
limits: Paths being available to the base model does not prove RL adds nothing at larger scale.
agent_relevance: Distilled traces add skill; RL on the same model mostly does not. Our agent cannot distil, so it should rely on search plus verification.

source: Shao et al. (2025) Spurious Rewards: Rethinking Training Signals in RLVR
finding: RLVR with random, incorrect-label or weak rewards still lifts Qwen2.5-Math-7B on MATH-500 almost as much as ground truth.
numbers: MATH-500 absolute gain: ground truth +29.1 points, random reward +21.4 points. Similar trend on AMC and AIME.
limits: Effect tied to Qwen2.5-Math; the middle reward types are in a figure I did not read cell by cell.
agent_relevance: Part of RLVR gain is not learning to be right. Beware reading benchmark gains as skill gains.

source: Shao et al. (2025) Spurious Rewards: Rethinking Training Signals in RLVR
finding: Mechanism and boundary: GRPO clipping bias amplifies high-prior behaviours. In Qwen2.5-Math-7B that is 'code reasoning' (Python-style reasoning without execution). Other families gain nothing.
numbers: Code reasoning frequency 65% to over 90%. Answers with it 60.9% accurate vs 28.0% without. Spurious rewards give minimal gain or loss on Qwen2.5, OLMo2 and Llama3.
limits: One 7B model analysed in depth.
agent_relevance: Eliciting a latent habit (code-like steps) can double accuracy; a scaffold can request that habit directly.

source: Wang et al. (2025) RL for Reasoning in LLMs with One Training Example
finding: One training example under RLVR lifts Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B nearly as much as 1.2k examples. Includes a format-correction baseline.
numbers: MATH500 36.0% to 73.6%; six-benchmark average 17.6% to 35.7% (7.0% gain beyond format); 1.2k DeepScaleR subset gives 73.6 and 35.9; two examples 74.8 and 36.6. Also works on Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, with GRPO and PPO.
limits: Authors say much of the early gain is format correction; effect is post-saturation, not fully explained.
agent_relevance: RL mostly elicits and formats what exists; exploration and format matter more than data volume.
quote: sustained test performance improvement even after the training accuracy has saturated

source: Yu et al. (2025) DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
finding: Open reproduction of R1-style RL on Qwen2.5-32B base. Naive GRPO got 30 on AIME 2024 vs DeepSeek's 47; four fixes (Clip-Higher, Dynamic Sampling, token-level loss, overlong reward shaping) reach 50.
numbers: AIME 2024: naive GRPO 30, R1-Zero-Qwen-32B 47, DAPO 50 with 50% of training steps.
limits: One base model and one main benchmark; AIME has 30 problems so one problem is 3.3 points.
agent_relevance: Entropy collapse and noisy rewards blocked reproduction; R1 numbers needed unreported details.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners
finding: Under identical RL on Countdown, Qwen-2.5-3B far exceeds Llama-3.2-3B. Qwen naturally shows four behaviours (verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining); Llama does not.
numbers: End of RL: Qwen about 60% accuracy vs Llama 30%.
limits: One task, 3B models; behaviours counted by an LLM classifier.
agent_relevance: These four behaviours map onto scaffold operators; a prompt demanding them could imitate the useful part.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners
finding: Priming Llama with synthetic traces containing these behaviours before RL closes the gap. The behaviour pattern matters, not correctness: incorrect solutions with good structure work about as well.
numbers: Primed Llama matches or exceeds Qwen. Transfer to MATH: 38% to 50% accuracy (own prompt format), 44% to 50% (Qwen 4-shot format); backtracking 0.15 to 0.59, verification 0.02 to 0.29.
limits: Correct vs incorrect comparison done on Countdown only.
agent_relevance: The form of reasoning, not the right answer, is what RL amplifies. Scaffold should enforce verify, back up, subgoal.

source: Liu et al. (2025) ProRL: Prolonged RL Expands Reasoning Boundaries in LLMs
finding: Counter to c09 and c10: prolonged RL (KL control, reference-policy resets, 136K problems in five domains, about 16k GPU hours) on a 1.5B distilled model raises pass@k even where the base fails at every k.
numbers: Versus DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B: pass@1 +14.7% math, +13.9% code, +54.8% logic puzzles, +25.1% STEM, +18.1% instruction following; beats domain-specialised baselines by +4.6% math and +6.5% code.
limits: Start model is already RL-distilled; gains track how weak the base was on the task. Not a clean base-vs-RL test.
agent_relevance: Boundary expansion looks possible with long training; background only for a no-training agent.

source: Moonshot AI (2025) Kimi k1.5: Scaling RL with LLMs
finding: Independent lab RL recipe with no MCTS, value function or PRM. RL context window scaled to 128k with partial rollouts. Long2short methods move long-CoT skill into short-CoT models.
numbers: Long-CoT: AIME 77.5, MATH-500 96.2, Codeforces 94th percentile, MathVista 74.9. Short-CoT: AIME 60.8, MATH-500 94.6, LiveCodeBench 47.3.
limits: Self-reported; closed model. The up-to-550% claim is versus GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.5 on short-CoT.
agent_relevance: Context length is a scaling axis; long2short shows thinking can be compressed, relevant to our token budget.

source: Lambert et al. (2024) Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
finding: Coined the name RLVR: replace the reward model with a verification function that returns a constant reward when the answer is right (math answer match, IFEval constraint check). Last stage after SFT and DPO.
numbers: RLVR improves GSM8K, MATH and IFEval while keeping other benchmarks about level; policies of 8B, 70B and 405B trained.
limits: I could not cleanly extract per-stage numbers from the PDF text. Lower KL penalty led to over-optimisation on IFEval constraints.
agent_relevance: RLVR is framed as the successor to STaR-style bootstrapping; useful only on checkable tasks, as is a verifier-gated scaffold.

source: Wu et al. (2025) Reasoning or Memorization? Unreliable Results of RL Due to Data Contamination
finding: Failed-replication angle on spurious rewards: Qwen2.5 appears contaminated on MATH-500, AMC and AIME (partial-prompt tests: can it finish the problem text or answer from half a prompt). On a leak-free generated set (RandomCalculation), only accurate rewards give steady gains; random rewards do not.
numbers: Benchmarks used: MATH-500 (500), AMC (83), AIME24 (30), AIME25 (30), LiveMathBench (100), Minerva (272). Exact completion rates not extracted.
limits: Contamination evidence is indirect; the arithmetic generator is a narrow task.
agent_relevance: Gains on models with leaked test sets are unreliable. Use fresh items for any scaffold-vs-baseline claim.

source: Wu et al. (2025) The Invisible Leash? Why RLVR May or May Not Escape Its Origin
finding: Empirical support dynamics: question-by-question match of verified successes before and after RLVR. More questions lose a verified success than gain one at the stated sampling budgets, even as pass@1 rises.
numbers: Shrinkage outweighs expansion across the evaluated aggregates; some RLVR models raise token-level entropy while lowering final-answer entropy. Exact counts not extracted.
limits: Claim is conditional on sampling budget and on current practice.
agent_relevance: Aggregate accuracy hides lost solutions; diverse sampling in a scaffold keeps alternatives that tuned models drop.

source: Huan et al. (2025) Does Math Reasoning Improve General LLM Capabilities? Understanding Transferability of LLM Reasoning
finding: Tested 20+ open reasoning-tuned models: most math gains do not transfer to other reasoning, coding, agent planning or instruction following. Controlled test on Qwen3-14B-Base with math-only data: RL transfers, SFT on teacher traces forgets.
numbers: RL-on-math models gain across reasoning and non-reasoning tasks; SFT-on-math shows limited transfer and drift (one task average in the figure is -5.6).
limits: Controlled part is one base model; figure values only partly read.
agent_relevance: RL-learned reasoning keeps general skills; SFT-distilled behaviours may be narrow, a warning for copying distilled traces.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
finding: Absolute Zero Reasoner: the model proposes its own code reasoning tasks and a code executor verifies them, giving verifiable reward with no human data. Beats zero models trained on tens of thousands of curated examples.
numbers: Coder-model gains grow with scale: +5.7 (3B), +10.2 (7B), +13.2 (14B) points.
limits: Executor limits tasks to code deduction, abduction and induction.
agent_relevance: Propose-then-verify with an executor is a loop usable at test time without training.

source: Bensal et al. (2025) Reflect, Retry, Reward: Self-Improving LLMs via RL
finding: Agent-loop form of RLVR: after a failed attempt the model writes a self-reflection, retries with it in context, and only the reflection tokens are rewarded if the retry succeeds. Binary feedback only.
numbers: Up to +34.7% on Countdown equation writing and +18.1% on APIGen function calling; 1.5B to 7B tuned models beat same-family models 10x larger.
limits: Needs a binary verifier and a second attempt; two tasks.
agent_relevance: Template for a fail, reflect, retry state loop; the prompt-only version can be tested without training.

source: Shao et al. (2024) DeepSeekMath (GRPO)
finding: GRPO drops the critic; baseline is the mean reward of a sampled group. RL improved Maj@K but not Pass@K already in this paper, so the 2025 pass@k debate (c09) was foreshadowed.
numbers: Numbers recorded in evidence_a.jsonl a03 and a04 (GSM8K 82.9 to 88.2, MATH 46.8 to 51.7).
limits: Not re-opened this session; I downloaded it but did not read it, so marked opened false.
agent_relevance: Sharpening, not widening, is an old finding.
